d tiffany.note: Vancouver DJ/producer (Sophie Sweetland), founder of the label Planet Euphorique — ranges from ambient and deep house to techno and breakbeat, frequent Roza Terenzi collaborator.

regularfantasy.note: Vancouver DJ/producer and a trailblazer for women and non-binary DJs in that city's scene — D. Tiffany's longtime Plush Management collaborator.

tottie.note: Dublab-affiliated LA radio host and co-founder of SOS Music, a !K7-backed label/platform spotlighting women and non-binary electronic artists.

ken ishii.note: Japanese techno pioneer since the mid-90s R&S Records run — 'Extra,' with its Koji Morimoto (Akira)-directed video, is a genre touchstone; now releases on his own 70 Drums imprint. A real legacy booking.

phara.note: Brussels DJ, a Fuse resident since 2016 — vinyl-only sets pulling from Detroit/Berlin/UK techno plus post-punk and EBM, runs the Phaaar label.

ynoti.note: LA techno DJ/producer (Sydney J) with classical-violin training — dark, driving techno; has shared bills with Truncate and SPFDJ, a rising local name.

olive kimoto.note: LA-born DJ/multimedia artist and KCRW host (NTS's Liquid Mirror) who also sings in trip-hop band Locust — sets move through downtempo, techno, synthpop and ambient; has shared bills with Jon Hopkins and Jenny Hval.

jason bentley.note: KCRW's longtime music director and Metropolis host — a tastemaker DJ who's shaped the station's house/downtempo/global sound for decades; a known quantity if you've listened to KCRW at all.

nap mx.note: Daniel Rincón — Colombian-born, Vancouver/Montreal-raised (1080p/Mood Hut crew) producer now based in Mexico City; blends Latin club, cumbia/sonidero and dubby ambient techno, and runs the ACA label focused on South American electronic music.

hashman deejay.note: Tanner Matt — Vancouver deep-house/dub producer in the Mood Hut orbit (collaborates with PLO Man, Pender Street Steppers); raw, outsider house and ambient dub, deliberately low-profile — no interviews, lets the records talk.

john.note: London two-piece — John Newton (drums/vocals) and Johnny Healey (guitar), both named John — self-managed, self-released post-punk duo built on volume and simplicity rather than polish.

french perfume.note: LA indie-rock band; thin public footprint beyond a handful of singles ('Bonnie') — a smaller local opener, not a known quantity.

maxi meraki.note: Maxim Defrancq — Brussels producer in the melodic-house/indie-dance lane, recently signed to CAA and running his own Radiate label; genuine cosigns from Solomun, Adriatique, Black Coffee and Keinemusik, releases via Diynamic and Higher Ground.

azure.note: LA-based DJ (raised in NY) amplifying African, Caribbean and Asian diaspora sounds — founder of the queer party series Lemon Pepper and the East-Asian-diasporic night Sinoclub.

black v neck.note: Miami house duo (since 2017) with genuine festival-scale reach — remixes and collabs with AFROJACK, Chris Lake and Green Velvet; big-room over underground.

dillon nathaniel.note: LA tech-house producer, Icon Collective grad, who co-wrote John Summit's breakout 'Esa Boca'; releases on Sola, Relief and Desert Hearts, known for thick basslines and hypnotic grooves.

sorry not jomari.note: LA local billing himself around a 'mischief house' sound — Academy LA/Avalon support slots and an independent 'We're Not Sorry' imprint, but a thin track record beyond that.

nicole gallamini.note: Caracas-born, Miami-based tech-house DJ/producer and Club Space regular who's shared bills with Adam Beyer, Loco Dice, Green Velvet and Stacey Pullen; runs her own Élevé label/brand, debut EP 'Haute Musique' in 2025.

adam ten and mita gami.note: Tel Aviv production duo behind the Maccabi House label/imprint — this party IS their own brand, built on groovy, melodic house with funky/indie-dance and organic textures rather than straight peak-time techno.

meatbodies.note: Chad Ubovich's garage-psych band, on In The Red Records — he's also in Fuzz with Ty Segall and Charles Moothart and spent years on bass with Mikal Cronin. Loud, fuzzed-out, riff-first.

mousse t.note: German house veteran (Mustafa Gündoğdu) — founded Peppermint Jam Records in '93, best known for 'Horny '98' and co-writing Tom Jones' 'Sex Bomb.' Uplifting, filter-y house — more pop-crossover than underground, but a legit long-running name.

soul clap.note: Boston/NY house duo (Eli Goldstein & Charles Levine) — House of EFUNK is literally their own decade-plus-running party brand, built on funky, eclectic house/disco/boogie rather than one straight lane; longtime Wolf + Lamb/Crew Love crowd.

yoshiki.note: X Japan's drummer/pianist/composer — this is his classical-crossover solo mode, orchestral reworkings of his own rock material, not a full band show. A genuine outlier from the house/techno lane, but a rare thing to catch live in a room like Disney Hall.

lovefingers.note: Andrew Hogge — LA-based Balearic/disco digger and 'shaman' of ESP Institute, the label/party he's run for two decades; a longtime DJ Harvey collaborator in the same cosmic-disco lineage. A real deep-crate booking, not filler.

driveways.note: Massachusetts pop-punk trio touring on raw, hook-heavy songs like 'Fifteen Minutes' — headlining this all-ages Teragram stop.

like roses.note: Berkeley emo/pop-punk band whose 2023 single 'Easy' broke out (1M+ streams); direct support on this tour.

action adventure.note: Touring pop-punk band rounding out the bill alongside Like Roses on this Driveways run.

black cat coalition.note: Queer post-grunge/experimental-punk band (Moose Campellone, Raven Abraham, Razz Myers, Sage Campellone) — noisy, DIY energy that fits The Smell's room.

mansaf mama.note: LA/NYC-based Syrian-Palestinian DJ who plays 'Global Sha3bi' — Arabic pop and shaabi plus Armenian, Assyrian and Kurdish music — tied directly to the Mahragan party series (sister event to the Bay Area's Kousa).

sarita linda.note: LA-based trans DJ on the same SWANA-diaspora party circuit as this bill; thinly documented beyond that.

miro stereokitchen.note: Regular Sunday Sessions LA resident/opener — house and deep-house vinyl sets, frequently played alongside Krane at this same series.

dor danino.note: Tel Aviv selector working a disco/funk/psychedelia-tinged house sound — championed and co-signed by Solomun and Dixon, which puts him right in the Innervisions-adjacent melodic-house pocket.

the femcels.note: London electronic-pop duo (Rowan Please and Gabriella Turton) — sharp, hyper-online club-pop that's more art-project than band.

dance arts center.note: LA producer Nicolette Norgaard's genre-bending solo project — synth-heavy dance music with theatrical songwriting, closer to Daft Punk-meets-Sondheim than a straight club act.

cfcf.note: Montreal's Michael Silver — Grammy-nominated remixer whose catalog runs Balearic disco to ambient/new-age; a genuinely deep, tasteful producer, not a typical rave booking.

figurine.note: James Tamborello's (Postal Service, Dntel) slowcore-electropop trio on Morr Music — gentle, hushed electronic pop, an unusual and interesting name on a free TBA-location bill.

the sound chalk makes.note: Mumbai-raised, London-based producer mixing noisy electroclash with bedroom-pop intimacy — young, buzzy, and stylistically restless.

amal nemer.note: Miami-based tech-house DJ/producer on Moon Harbour and Glasgow Underground — percussion-driven house pulling from Damian Lazarus and Martinez Brothers; solidly in the groovier end of tech-house.

solardo.note: Mark Richards and James Eliot — UK tech-house duo behind Sola Records and Wild Culture, XOYO/fabric residency pedigree; funky, jacking house that's a straight match for the fabric-London end of the lane.

john early.note: Comedian/actor (Search Party, Hacks) making his feature directorial debut here — he also stars, so expect arch, hyper-stylized satire rather than straight comedy.

asco.note: East LA Chicano art collective (Harry Gamboa Jr., Gronk, Willie Herrón, Patssi Valdez) known for guerrilla street performance and conceptual art in the '70s-'80s — foundational and under-known LA art history.

ty segall.note: Prolific garage-rock/psych musician (Fuzz, GØGGS, a dozen-plus solo LPs) — this is him DJing rather than playing, so expect a record-collector's grab-bag, not a live band.

raxon.note: Barcelona-based (Egyptian-born) melodic/stripped-back techno producer on Diynamic, Cocoon, and Kompakt — solid European club pedigree.

john bryars.note: LA local, eclectic acid/techno/electro/EBM selector who's played A Club Called Rhonda and Boiler Room — a good bet for a genuinely varied warm-up set.

alejandro gonzález iñárritu.note: Mexican director's 2000 debut — three interlocking stories triggered by a Mexico City car crash; launched Gael García Bernal and the whole Iñárritu/del Toro/Cuarón wave internationally.

shonky.note: Paris house/tech-house lifer (Olivier Ducreux) — a third of the Apollonia trio with Dan Ghenacia and Dyed Soundorom; groovy, stripped-back underground house, well-suited to an extended set.

silky.note: London house/techno DJ mentored by Frankie Knuckles — works the grey zone between deep house and techno, with releases on Culprit and My Favorite Robot.

enzo muro.note: Peruvian-born, LA-based house/techno selector and a resident of Dialogue itself — patient, flow-first sets; also co-runs the vinyl-only YouKnowWhat label/party.

geneva jacuzzi.note: LA underground synth-pop fixture since the mid-2000s (Dais Records) — theatrical, lo-fi cold-wave pop with a strong performance-art bent; came up alongside Ariel Pink in that scene.

lee foss.note: Chicago-schooled house lifer out of DeKalb, IL — co-founded Hot Creations with Jamie Jones and later launched Repopulate Mars; a real name in modern underground house, not just a big-festival booking.

henry pope.note: Venice Beach-based producer running his own Genius Loci/Fresh Tracks/Sense labels — Beatport #1 indie-dance and afro-house releases, sets that fold in live musicians.

hazy.note: Recurring Sunday Sessions LA resident — vinyl-only house sets, a regular on the rotation at the series' open-airs.

tortoise.note: Chicago post-rock institution since the early '90s (Thrill Jockey) — instrumental, dub- and krautrock-informed, built on groove and texture more than riffs; a genuine legacy act for the small-venue experimental/indie lane.

tara jane o neil.note: Louisville scene vet (ex-Rodan, Retsin) turned solo artist — hushed, drone-leaning indie-folk/experimental songwriting, closer to Grouper or Low than a rock set; a quiet, well-matched opener.

artur us.note: LA vinyl selector and a regular in the Certified Groovers rotation — deep, warm house, all-wax sets.

gilbert0.note: Another Certified Groovers regular — same all-vinyl deep-house lane, secret-location DTLA parties.

bob moses.note: Vancouver-born, LA-based duo (Tom Howie & Jimmy Vallance) — moody, dance-inflected indie-electronic, best known for 'Tearing Me Up'; the live-band, electronic-adjacent tier rather than a DJ set.

cannons.note: LA synth-pop trio best known for the viral 'Fire for You' — dreamy, retro-tinged synth/disco pop, lighter and poppier than Bob Moses.

agraybé.note: LA/Minnesota DJ (Ariana Gray Bé), part of the Made to Move orbit — psychedelic, groove-forward house selections; releases via Kajunga.

akumen.note: Chinatown-based LA house/techno/disco DJ-producer and Made to Move co-founder — releases on Fortune Signal and Juke Bounce Werk, played BBC Radio 1, Rinse FM, and NTS.

invt.note: Miami duo (Luca Medici & Delbert Perez) — sound-system club music fusing dub, UK bass, and Latin-rooted percussion; play DC-10/Circoloco, Fabric, and Panorama Bar.

papa lu.note: Bay Area-to-LA DJ/producer spanning disco to techno, Kazbah (Burning Man) co-founder — plays everything from underground rooms to EDC/Escape-tier festivals.

stacy christine.note: LA warehouse-scene DJ since 2012 (Music For Dancers, Critter Control, Machine Club lineage) — joyful house into kinetic techno; has opened for DJ Harvey, Moodymann, and Honey Dijon.

dj kerry.note: LA DJ since 2005, longtime Dublab radio host and founder of The Basement, a membership-based party rooted in Paradise Garage/West Coast warehouse tradition.

einmusik.note: Berlin producer (Samuel Kindermann), runs Einmusika Recordings since 2008 — emotive, melodic house/techno; his Cercle livestream from Norway has 15M+ views.

emperor x.note: Chad Matheny's long-running solo project (since 1998, Berlin-based since 2012) — fuses the punk-songwriter tradition of Billy Bragg with tape-loop minimalism; new album 'Unified Field' due summer 2026 on Bar/None.

clovers daughter.note: Noor Shami's indie-pop/alt project, American-Palestinian singer-songwriter — raw, lyric-forward storytelling; debut full-length 'Am I Worth It?' out August 2025.

miss capri.note: LA house/techno DJ known for groovy, sultry sets around the Nico's Wine Bar/Baby Battista circuit.

est dani.note: LA house/techno DJ in the same groovy, sultry-set lane as the rest of the Nico's Wine Bar circuit.

lily ardalan.note: Native Angeleno DJ and event producer — genre-fluid house/techno sets, resident at Girl Math, Aftermidnight, and Nico's Wine Bar.

ben böhmer.note: German producer on Anjunadeep — melodic/progressive house, tours with a live band rather than just decks; same Anjuna-orbit lane as Lane 8 and Yotto, a genuinely good opener for this bill.

juliet mendoza.note: LA-native house DJ and dancer — founder/resident of Jill's House (Jackin Jills), a Defected 'Unsung Heroes' alum; melodic, soulful, deep house rooted in the city's Black/Latin house dance lineage.

van dyke parks.note: Legendary orchestral pop arranger/songwriter — co-wrote the Beach Boys' unfinished 'Smile' and has been Randy Newman's longtime arranger; a genuine California pop institution, not a nostalgia act.

inara george.note: LA singer-songwriter (The Bird and the Bee, daughter of Little Feat's Lowell George) — she and Parks made the warm, orchestral 2008 duo album 'An Invitation' together, which this pairing draws on.

dj spinna.note: Brooklyn crate-digging legend (Jigmastas, BBE's 'Beat Generation' compilation series) beloved for deep funk/soul/hip-hop sets; a genuinely serious digger fronting this free Stevie Wonder tribute, not a casual bill.

jacques greene.note: Montreal producer on LuckyMe — emotive, R&B-inflected UK garage and bass (see 'Ready', 'Another Girl'); moody and vocal-chopped, more feeling than functional peak-time.

2d0gs.note: LA duo (SEES00000 & J!MMY) — newer name prepping a 2026 EP for dh2; plugged into the same LuckyMe-adjacent scene but still an unknown quantity live.

bahar khadem.note: LA selector behind the Direct Drive party series — a self-described 'Chicago soul' deep house/club-music digger who's shared bills with Ariel Zetina and Introspekt on the DTLA warehouse circuit.

teed.note: Totally Enormous Extinct Dinosaurs — UK producer Orlando Higginbottom, glossy nu-disco/synth-pop ('Trouble', 'Household Name'); shiny and danceable, not a deep-digger set.

kindness.note: Adam Bainbridge — London songwriter/producer steeped in disco, funk and R&B (collabs with Robyn, Blood Orange, Kelela); DJs in the same warm, groove-forward lane as his records.

shaun ross.note: Model known for breaking barriers in fashion who's become a recurring guest/performer at Rhonda parties — more scene presence than DJ set, so treat as texture on the bill.

bianca lexis.note: LA dublab/NTS host (Panorama Heaven) and Rhonda regular — genre-bending sets running '80s synth-pop and new wave into boogie, house and italo.

goddollars.note: Loren Granich — Rhonda's own co-founder/resident, playing the sexy house-and-disco sound the party was built around.

sincerely manolo.note: LA DJ/producer (Manny Lateulade) digging into underground house, disco and global club sounds; also a visual artist, has played EDC, Coachella's Sahara, and LA Pride.

luigi amore.note: Recurring name on LA pool/rooftop day-party bills like Sex with The City — not enough reliably sourced info to characterize the sound with confidence.

evo twinz.note: LA duo billed as melodic-techno/tribal producers — a support-tier name on this recurring series, thinly documented beyond that.

tone ranger.note: Santa Fe-based live electronic act blending classic Americana instrumentation with house and ambient textures — a live hybrid rather than a DJ set.

tonoso.note: LA live-electronic/indie-dance duo — thinly documented online, so treat this billing with lower confidence.

alan fitzpatrick.note: UK techno heavyweight and founder of We Are The Brave — driving, peak-time techno that tours the same circuit as Adam Beyer/Drumcode-tier bills; a legit headliner in the European techno lane.

anastasia giovani.note: SoCal-raised, now a fixture of LA's underground techno scene (SXTCY resident, founder of the VSCRL event series) — dark, textured, experimental techno sets.

greg downey.note: Belfast-born DJ/producer and founder of the Skullduggery label — started in trance (his 'Stadium' was Mixmag's Cream Ibiza anthem of 2008) before moving into deeper underground techno via his R.I.C.O alias.

gun outfit.note: Olympia-turned-LA psych/post-punk band on Post Present Medium since their 2008 debut EP — a foundational act for the label being celebrated.

the spatulas.note: Bloomington, IN lo-fi punk band on the Post Present Medium roster.

chronophage.note: Austin DIY punk four-piece with a sophisticated, transgressive songwriting bent — two LPs and a run of cassettes deep.

guiding light.note: Austin punk band singing bilingually in German/English over jangly, hyper-strummed garage — their debut LP just came out on Post Present Medium.

semi trucks.note: LA art-pop project fronted by Brendan Sepe, grown from a solo bedroom effort into a full band — scrappy, melodic songs.

muscle beach.note: LA four-piece delivering noisy, scattershot 'party band' improvisations — a Smell regular.

kate hall.note: No Age/Mika Miko/Dunes-adjacent LA musician (half of the News Feeds project with Luke Fischbeck & Dean Spunt) DJing the night.

iwrotehaikusaboutcannibalisminyouryearbo.note: Bay Area screamo band (Antioch, CA) from the mid-2000s skramz wave, broken up 2007, reactivated in 2020 — a real scene-history booking for genre diehards, outside the digest's usual electronic/rock lane.

loma prieta.note: Long-running Bay Area screamo band (since 2004) — a foundational, still-active name in the skramz revival, chaotic and dissonant.

nuvolascura.note: LA screamo/mathcore four-piece (formerly Vril) blending skramz with technical, dissonant hardcore — one of the genre's current top-tier acts.

clay birds.note: Couldn't confidently verify which band this billing refers to (conflicting bios online) — leaving uncharacterized rather than guessing.

the stitches.note: OC garage-punk institution since 1994 — snotty, high-energy '70s-style punk in the Rip Off Records/Dirtnap lane, one of the scene's most volatile, fun live acts.

goose.note: Connecticut jam band (formed 2014) with a devoted, Phish-adjacent live following built on lengthy improvisation — outside the usual electronic/indie lane here but a real, well-loved live act, and the Greek is a favorite room. (Note: 'jam-band' isn't yet in the subgenre vocab; flagging rather than inventing a tag.)

bass drum of death.note: Mississippi-born fuzzy garage-rock project (John Barrett) on Fat Possum — hooky, loud, Black Lips/Wavves-adjacent.

memo pst.note: LA punk band formed 2022 by Orville Neeley (Bad Sports, OBN IIIs) and Chris Shaw (Ex-Cult) — raw, primitive punk on In The Red, recorded at John Dwyer's Discount Mirrors studio.

black moth super rainbow.note: Tobacco-fronted Pittsburgh outfit — vocoder-heavy, hazy psychedelic pop over fuzzed analog synths; a cult-favorite band, not a nostalgia act despite the vintage-synth sound. ('Psych' isn't yet in the subgenre vocab; flagging rather than coining a tag.)

giant day.note: Elephant 6-affiliated post-punk/art-rock duo (Derek Almstead of Olivia Tremor Control/of Montreal + Emily Growden) — psych-funk, synth-forward; the first official new E6 band in 15+ years.

dreya v.note: Bay Area DJ/producer (formerly MISS DRE) — vocal-forward tech house/melodic house crossover on labels like REALM and Octopus; been turning up in Gorgon City's sets lately.

andrey pushkarev.note: Russian DJ/producer (25+ years in) and founder of the Luck of Access label — melodic, melancholic deep house, dub techno and ambient; a genuine deep-selector name, not a festival booking.

taimur.note: NY/Miami-based DJ-producer (Taimur Agha), co-founder of Blkmarket Membership — earned a fabric London debut off the strength of his sets; house-techno crossover with real European club credibility.

abe vigoda.note: LA experimental/'tropical punk' band from the mid-2000s Smell scene, on Post Present Medium — jittery, humid, post-punk-meets-tropicalia; this run is a reunion set for the label's anniversary.

callahan and witscher.note: NYC duo of two veteran underground experimentalists (Jack Callahan, aka die Reihe; Jeff Witscher, aka Rene Hell) whose new project is a surprising, hooky pivot toward songs after years of noise/ambient work.

debt rag.note: Olympia, WA punk trio (former members of Grass Widow and Girlsperm) playing guitarless, clattering, drum-and-keyboard punk — Post Present Medium's 2023 LP 'Lost to the Fantasy.'

the intima.note: Portland post-punk quartet, violin-driven, active 1999-2004 and recently reunited — shared stages with The Rapture and The Mekons back in the day; PPM reissued their 'Peril and Panic' LP.

tomahawk.note: Mike Patton's avant-metal band with Duane Denison (Jesus Lizard) and John Stanier (Helmet) — angular, riff-heavy, weirder than a typical supergroup.

melvins.note: Legendary Washington sludge/noise-rock band (formative influence on Nirvana/grunge) — decades-deep, still genuinely heavy and strange live.

jks.note: French DJ/producer (Valentin De Sieter) based in Berlin — percussive, hypnotic techno that draws on UK bass and broken techno; cites Randomer as a direct influence.

randomer.note: North London producer (Rohan Walder), one of the more prolific UK techno names of the last decade — releases on Hessle Audio, L.I.E.S. and Numbers; deep, spatial techno that pulls in dubstep and garage markers.

11ai.note: LA electronic/hyperpop-adjacent artist — just released the full-length 'Leap Year Register' (June 2026); glitchy, maximalist pop production.

sfv acid.note: LA producer Zane Reynolds — funky, acid-house-and-electro-funk hybrid out of the San Fernando Valley since 2007; his debut EP was Post Present Medium's very first vinyl release, and he's a longtime Dublab resident.

ava blank.note: LA electronic producer (BIOTEAM, dead nokia, Kaiyosky, ravemail) working across house, IDM, downtempo and UK garage.

of montreal.note: Kevin Barnes' long-running glam/psych-pop project (Elephant 6-adjacent) — decades of records and theatrical, costumed live shows.

sloppy jane.note: Haley Dahl's theatrical art-rock project — best known for recording the album 'Madison' inside an actual cave with a 30-piece ensemble; strange, ambitious orchestral rock.

adam ten.note: Israeli-born, Amsterdam-based producer — half of Adam Ten & Mita Gami, the melodic house/techno duo who took over Coachella's Yuma Tent two weekends running in 2024; co-founder of the Maccabi House movement.

mita gami.note: The other half of Adam Ten & Mita Gami — driving melodic house crossed with funk and indie-dance; Maccabi House is literally their own brand/label.

momma.note: Brooklyn duo-fronted band (Etta Friedman, Allegra Weingarten) doing loving, well-executed 90s alt-rock/grunge revival — Polyvinyl, breakout album 'Household Name.'

rocket.note: LA alt-rock band (formed 2021) with a shoegaze-leaning edge — recently opened arena dates for Smashing Pumpkins.

the womack sisters.note: LA soul trio (BG, Zeimani, Kucha) carrying serious family lineage — daughters of Cecil & Linda Womack, granddaughters of Sam Cooke, niece/nephews of Bobby Womack; debuting their self-titled Daptone Records album the same day as this show.

the beths.note: Auckland, NZ four-piece — sharp, hook-driven indie rock, consistently well-reviewed (Pitchfork/NPR) over several albums.

beach bunny.note: Chicago's Lili Trifilio-led indie-pop project — broke out with the viral 'Prom Queen,' has since grown into a full-band, hookier sound.

lovetempo.note: Solo disco project of Mattie Safer (bassist/singer of Poolside and The Rapture) — warm, romantic soul-disco-house; recent Airliner regular.

dj swisha.note: Philly-born, LA-raised, NYC-based member of the Juke Bounce Werk crew and Fool's Gold Records signee — juke, footwork and Jersey/Baltimore club lineage; one of the more rhythmically restless names on the underground circuit.

mapamota.note: LA DJ and event producer (behind Direct Drive, Serenity Link, Soul Swap) — house, afrobeats, techno and global club rhythms, built around percussive, high-energy sets.

strange case.note: LA rock band, road-tested over 8+ years of SoCal gigging — KROQ 'Locals Only' airplay and a Netflix sync (The Lincoln Lawyer); dropping a new album, 'Gone For a While,' the day before this show.

danny tenaglia.note: NYC house/techno institution from the Twilo/Vinyl (ex-Sound Factory) era — famous for tribal, driving, hours-long marathon sets that build slow and never let up. A legitimate legend headlining a pier day party.

cid.note: Touring tech-house DJ/producer with a run of releases on Lee Foss's Repopulate Mars — big-room but genuinely well-selected festival tech-house, the headliner of this bill.

tobehonest.note: LA-based tech-house DJ/producer on the come-up — Latin-groove/hip-hop-inflected sound with Beatport Top 100 releases and cosigns from Chris Lake and John Summit; regular at Exchange LA/Sound/Academy.

juos.note: LA producer working a Latin tech-house lane — reggaeton and Latin rhythmic elements folded into tech-house, festival-circuit booking (Day Trip, Insomniac-adjacent).

cat and maomi.note: Texas-born, now LA-based DJ duo — sexy, groove-heavy techno/house that's played the Palladium, Sound, EDC and Day Trip; more festival-mainstage than underground selector.

cynthia rothrock.note: American martial artist-turned-actress who became one of the only Western stars to break into 1980s Hong Kong action cinema — co-lead opposite Michelle Yeoh here.

bl suede.note: Inglewood-born electronic-soul DJ/producer/singer, MON€¥CAT resident — blends Afro-house, deep tech and soul into hybrid sets with live vocals; has released with Kevin Saunderson and on Armada.

mana moves.note: Recurring Westside Bounce billing — couldn't verify a fuller bio beyond that circuit.

mad gavs.note: LA DJ/producer who cut her teeth on UCLA Radio — genuinely versatile across club, breaks, house, techno, jersey and jungle; part of the Lots of Practice label crew, has opened for A-Trak and Flava D.

nacocamellia.note: LA-based DJ/designer active on the local circuit — couldn't verify a fuller bio or genre lane.

starsdontmeananything.note: Long Beach/Oakland screamo-hardcore band (Adam Smith, Sasha Guleff, Cheianne Armstrong, Eric Mulliniks) on No Time Records — latest LP 'Fire Is Beautiful' (2025).

jane monheit.note: Grammy-nominated jazz vocalist whose phrasing gets compared to Ella Fitzgerald — a Great American Songbook specialist, not an experimental pick.

max haymer.note: LA jazz pianist and Monheit's longtime music director; a Sam First regular who's essentially built a home base in this room rather than just backing her for the night.

parts and labor.note: Brooklyn noise-rock band (2002-2013, reunited this year with their first new album in 15 years) that plugged tunes into feedback the way Hüsker Dü and Mission of Burma did — scene-mates of Liars and Black Dice, melody first, noise as texture not the point.

hlllyh.note: New band from former Mae Shi members (Dan Chao, James Baker, Burt Hashiguchi), named after that band's acclaimed 2008 album — carries over The Mae Shi's LA art-punk/experimental-pop energy.

harmony holiday.note: LA poet, dancer, and archivist — daughter of soul singer-songwriter Jimmy Holiday, who died when she was five — whose books (Negro League Baseball, Go Find Your Father) and live performances work through jazz/soul history and Black avant-garde archives. Closer to a lecture-performance than a set.

ferry corsten.note: Dutch trance OG since the late-90s boom (System F, Gouryella with a young Tiësto) who now runs his own Flashover label and plays a broader, more contemporary progressive-leaning set. Real lineage in the genre, but this is Avalon's mainstream Friday circuit, not an underground booking.

prince daddy and the hyena.note: Albany, NY emo/pop-punk band whose self-titled 2020 album swings from pop hooks to noisy freakouts and back — now on Pure Noise Records after stints on Counter Intuitive and Broken World Media.

macseal.note: Long Island (Farmingdale) band blending Midwest emo, math rock, and pop-punk; their last album was produced by Billy Mannino (Oso Oso), placing them in that same emo-revival circle.

angel bat dawid.note: Chicago clarinetist/vocalist on International Anthem — raw, ritualistic spiritual jazz descended from Sun Ra and the AACM.

georgia anne muldrow.note: LA soul/jazz producer-vocalist behind SomeOthaShip Connect — Dilla-indebted, deeply spiritual funk/jazz/hip-hop; has worked with Mos Def and Robert Glasper.

j cuuzi.note: Austin art-punk/electro group built around costumed, high-concept live shows — distorted guitars over pulsing electro beats; has opened for Viagra Boys and Warmduscher.

3371.note: Long Beach neo-grunge band — fuzzy, unpolished guitar rock; self-described 'neo grunge 4 loverz.'

john tejada.note: Vienna-born, LA-based since childhood — Palette Recordings founder and a fixture of musical, melodic techno/deep house since the mid-90s (Kompakt, Pokerflat, Cocoon). Real underground pedigree headlining his own night.

ian llorens.note: Certified Groovers resident, LA-based (Puerto Rico-born) — rhythm-forward house/techno selector, also plays as O God / Soundprism.

sky rivers.note: LA-native DJ since the acid-house '90s, cut his teeth in SF's scene in the 2000s — deep vinyl collector, a Sunday Sessions LA regular too.

zini us.note: LA-based selector (Syrian roots) working the lighter, groove-forward side of house/techno.

midnight magic.note: NYC nu-disco/boogie live band (Environ, Permanent Vacation), best known for 'Beam Me Up' — a real disco-revival name, well above what a birthday-party lineup usually lands.

dirtie blonde.note: LA disco DJ/producer — the Apotheke regular this party is thrown for.

fabiano do nascimento.note: Rio-born, LA-based nylon-string guitarist — Brazilian jazz woven with the city's experimental-jazz crowd (Leaving Records, Far Out, Now-Again); a Tiny Desk alum.

john carroll kirby.note: LA keyboardist/producer on Stones Throw (My Garden, Septet) — jazz/exotica solo records, plus session work for Frank Ocean, Solange and Steve Lacy.

tiki pasillas.note: Grammy-nominated SoCal multi-percussionist/drummer with decades of session credits — grounds the rhythm section here.

highkin.note: Moscow-born, LA-based vinyl collector/DJ — a regular in the Sunday Sessions LA rotation.

dance maniacs.note: LA trio blending house, breakbeat, electro and East Coast club edits — the party's own billing, and an accurate one; more scrappy rave energy than deep-house selectorship.

dj ligma.note: Groovers Ball resident (frequently b2b/b3b with Oscar Osorio); part of the crew's hard house/old-school-techno-leaning core since the party's 2023 founding.

oscar osorio.note: Groovers Ball resident, regularly paired with DJ LIGMA (they've released a joint EP together) — same bangin' rave/techno lane as the rest of the crew.

tedd patterson.note: NYC club legend who came up at Sound Factory and Cielo in the 90s — an eclectic, fusion-and-contrast house selector in the Body & Soul/Shelter lineage; his influence reaches Honey Dijon and The Illustrious Blacks.

jack faulkner.note: LA-based DJ/promoter (also a real-estate agent by day) who's spent years pushing soulful, deep, high-energy house on the West Coast — runs the AXIS open-air series this event belongs to.

jane schoenbrun.note: Director of this and I Saw the TV Glow — makes eerie, internet-native coming-of-age horror about identity dissolving into screens; one of the more distinctive indie voices of the last five years.

dave aju.note: SF producer (Marc Barrite) and longtime Circus Company artist — soulful, left-field minimal house built from his own vocals and samples; played Fabric, Panorama Bar and Rex Club. A genuinely deep booking for a free night.

isimo.note: LA selector said to come out of the city's early-90s underground house/techno and warehouse scene — couldn't independently verify further, so treat this one as unconfirmed.

john doe.note: Not in the official lineup list, only the title — likely a pseudonymous or mystery-guest booking rather than a specific known artist. Unconfirmed.

dj bone.note: Detroit techno lifer (Eric Dulan), founder of Subject Detroit — deep, hypnotic, no-filler techno from someone who's been doing it since the '90s underground scene.

stacey hotwaxx hale.note: Detroit house pioneer often called the 'Godmother of House' — spinning since the late '70s/'80s at clubs like Chessmate and Todd's, one of the first women behind the decks in the genre's birthplace.

force placement.note: LA techno DJ/producer (Jason James), co-founder of The Black Lodge collective/label — ranges soulful house to acid techno, a genuinely respected name in the local underground.

saand.note: LA DJ/producer (Michael Sandler), Beatport's 2015 Breakthrough Artist and head of the Tierra Sounds label — soulful, rhythm-forward house.

keyspan.note: LA producer/DJ, a resident at Sound Nightclub — the local support slot on this bill.

rimarkable.note: Detroit-rooted, LA-based house/techno DJ-producer and longtime host of the Defected Radio Show — soul/funk/disco-inflected sets, decks shared with Louie Vega and Honey Dijon.

audiojack.note: UK tech-house/house duo (Richard Burkinshaw & James Rial) — over a decade on Crosstown Rebels, Solid Grooves and Toolroom, deep/tech house with a UK-garage tinge.

rozalesd.note: SoCal deep house/tech-house duo, founders of the Momentos label and party series — respected locally, with support from Hot Since 82 and Franky Wah.

ameega.note: French modern-funk/boogie band leading the sound since 2002, billed stateside as "the last Mohican of boogie" — 80s-style synth-funk revivalism, a rare touring booking.

xl middleton.note: LA modern-funk mainstay and MoFunk Records founder — G-funk-inflected synth-boogie, part of the Funkmosphere/Broadway lineage.

moniquea.note: LA boogie-funk vocalist and XL Middleton's longtime collaborator on MoFunk — smooth G-funk/boogie in the Dam-Funk lineage.

novena carmel.note: Longtime KCRW DJ/host (Morning Becomes Eclectic) and singer — soulful, genre-crossing sets from a mainstay of LA's public-radio music scene.

dj michael donte.note: Host of Black House Radio — deep house and soul-leaning sets rooted in Black dance-music history.

oscar g.note: Miami house legend, one half of Murk (with Ralph Falcón) — tribal/deep house pioneer since the early '90s and longtime Space Miami resident.

wormwood star.note: LA alt-rock project active on the local DIY circuit (released "Rhapsody" in 2025) — thin footprint beyond that, so treat as a discovery booking.

royal coda.note: Sacramento-formed post-hardcore/prog outfit fronted by Kurt Travis (ex-Dance Gavin Dance) and guitarist Sergio Medina (ex-Stolas) — technical, proggy, screamo-adjacent.

tauceti.note: French techno/ambient producer with a growing profile in that scene — couldn't pin down a label home, so this reads more promising than proven.

joris voorn.note: Dutch mainstay of melodic techno-house since the mid-2000s (his own Green and Rejected labels) — the 'Nobody Knows' album won Billboard's Electronic Album of the Year in 2014. Widescreen, emotive, festival-capable; not on the tracked list but a real headliner, closer to Solomun/Tale of Us than pure techno.

luis miranda.note: Madrid-born, LA-based techno producer on Tronic and KD Raw — driving peak-time techno with real co-signs (Richie Hawtin, Rødhåd support his tracks); a legit local name, not filler support.

materielle.note: LA techno producer/DJ steeped in '90s Detroit — dub-heavy, hypnotic, texture-first sets; still building a catalog (Delusi EPs) but a thoughtful selector.

sultan shepard.note: Montreal-born, now LA-based progressive/melodic house duo (Ossama Al Sarraf & Ned Shepard) — Grammy-nominated for their Bruno Mars remix; steady, emotive mid-tempo sets since the early 2010s remix era rather than an underground name.

kasbo.note: Gothenburg producer on ODESZA's Foreign Family Collective — soulful, melody-rich electronic that leans future-bass/downtempo; softer and poppier than the rest of this bill.

qrion.note: Japan-born, Austin-based producer on Anjunadeep — shimmering, emotive melodic house; DJ Mag's 2021 Future Star, two albums deep with the label.

ashibah.note: Danish-Egyptian DJ/vocalist on Defected and Get Physical — deep/tech house built around her own live vocals; more pop-house crossover than underground selector.

a club called rhonda.note: LA's own queer disco/house institution (Loren Granic & Gregory Alexander) — the closest thing on this bill to the rooftop-groove lane, all disco edits and drag-flecked chaos rather than a band.

oliver koletzki.note: Hamburg-via-Berlin producer, founder of Stil vor Talent (20 years running) — his 2005 track 'Der Mückenschwarm' on Sven Väth's Cocoon helped define the melodic-house wave that came after. Big, emotive, festival-ready; closer to Dixon/Adriatique than deep underground.

aundreja.note: LA-born, Guatemalan-American DJ on the fast rise in the local hard techno/trance scene since her 2023 debut — hypnotic, spiritual, high-BPM sets, already playing Exchange LA, Avalon and EU dates (Rex Club Paris, E1 London).

paolo ferrara.note: Italian 'Heavy Destroyer' behind TechnoMetal — hard techno fused with metal aggression and industrial noise, co-founder of the HEX movement; his 'Last Resort' hit #1 on Beatport's Hard Techno chart in 2024. A much harder, more extreme booking than the rooftop-groove lane, closer to Sara Landry's crowd.

elise ember.note: LA 'second-generation' techno DJ working the local hard/heavy techno circuit (SXTCY, Closer.LA).

kristyle.note: LA hard techno/schranz DJ building a following in the local warehouse and afterhours scene.

boris.note: Longtime Berlin techno figure — SWXCH bills him as a Berghain/Panorama Bar resident, and this is his ongoing residency there (volume 7 now); decades of stripped-back, hypnotic techno for queer dancefloors. (Note: there's more than one touring 'Boris' — this bio follows SWXCH's own description of their resident.)

kittamami.note: Detroit-bred, LA-based DJ/producer blending house and techno with empowering vocal-driven tracks; active across the local warehouse scene.

afriqua.note: Adam Longman Parker — Virginia-born, Berlin-based producer on R&S Records; his 2019 LP 'Colored' fused deep house/techno with an explicit Black-culture lens. A genuinely respected, thoughtful name — arguably the most substantive booking on this bill.

azzecca.note: Chicago DJ/producer (Allie DeCastris) and COSIMEA label boss — cosmic, dark, disco-inflected house/techno; a Beatport 'Next Artist' for 2025 who's shared bills with Tale of Us and CamelPhat.

ray kash.note: LA underground fixture since 2010 (Temple Tuesdays resident) — deep house into techno and melodic, weaned on Danny Tenaglia/Jonathan Peters-style New York house.

warehouse preservation society.note: LA disco-house DJ duo (TK & Tavish) — dynamic, acid-tinged dancefloor energy; played Glastonbury, Love International and Sunset Campout, one half rooted in '90s SF underground, the other in Venice/Ocean Park hip-hop-to-house.

bears in space.note: The LA collective behind this very party — Chris Bowen and Victor Rodriguez have run it since 2009, one of the city's longest-standing queer disco/house day parties, historically pulling in guests like DJ Harvey and Horse Meat Disco.

perfect lovers.note: LA DJ (Celice Monnette) and co-founder of the Mexico City/LA queer warehouse party @pordetroitmx and the Muy Muy label — house and techno with a queer-community throughline.

rival consoles.note: Ryan Lee West — UK producer on Erased Tapes known for guitar-and-modular-laced, emotionally heavy electronic/ambient records ('Persona', 'Now Is'); closer to Jon Hopkins/Nils Frahm territory than a club DJ set.

khotin.note: Edmonton producer (Dylan Khotin-Foote) on Ghostly International — warm, hazy ambient-house; a gentle, textural opener.

carlita.note: Istanbul-born, classically trained (cello, Royal Academy of Music) DJ/producer — blends Turkish folk and classical sensibility into melodic house and subtle techno; signed to Ninja Tune/Counter Records, runs the Senza Fine party series alongside names like DJ Tennis. A genuinely musical selector, not just a functional house DJ.

anetha.note: French techno DJ/producer out of the Paris scene — raw, physical peak-time sets, a fixture of the current European festival-techno wave.

brutalismus 3000.note: German techno duo mixing 90s rave euphoria with hardgroove — part of the Berlin-adjacent revival crew getting big US festival bookings.

sammy virji.note: UK garage/bassline producer at the center of the current UKG resurgence.

confidence man.note: Australian dance-pop group with a theatrical, costumed live show — festival-circuit favorite, more pop spectacle than DJ set.

adam lucky.note: Numero Group's own in-house DJ — plays the reissue label's archive all-vinyl: disco, Italo and deep house, no laptop involved.

willis.note: Nashville-via-Alabama indie-rock project — warm, rhythmic, nostalgic songwriting; 2024 debut LP 'I Can't Thank You Enough.'

zzzahara.note: Highland Park's own Zahara Jaime (formerly half of the duo the Simps with Eyedress) — detailed, melodic indie that moves between shoegaze, post-punk and dream-pop.

the flooks.note: Newer indie-pop/alt-rock duo who broke via TikTok off a debut single; thin track record beyond that so far.

dj crenshaw.note: Name recurs around Sid The Cat and, separately, as a pre-show DJ credit at rooms like the Hollywood Bowl and Forest Hills Stadium — couldn't pin down a clean genre lane or bio; unverified.

robert bresson.note: French director (Pickpocket, Au Hasard Balthazar) known for austere, non-professional-actor 'models' and a spare, almost devotional style — A Man Escaped (1956) is one of his most acclaimed.

yeon sang ho.note: South Korean director of Train to Busan and the Netflix series Hellbound — genre horror with real social/political bite underneath the zombie mechanics.

agnieszka holland.note: Polish director (Europa Europa, In Darkness) known for confronting political and wartime subject matter head-on; Green Border tackles the Polish-Belarusian refugee crisis and was genuinely controversial in Poland.

monkey safari.note: German duo (Get Physical, Anjunadeep, Bedrock) making sunny, melodic organic house — run their own Hommage label and own a club in their hometown of Halle.

marques wyatt.note: West Coast deep house legend — ran LA's long-running Deep party/residency from the late '90s into the 2010s and is generally credited with helping put LA's dance scene on the map alongside NYC and Miami.

quarkestra.note: Touring silent-film orchestra (Denver-based) that writes original live scores for classic silent films — Häxan and Nosferatu are their regular touring pairing, played off audience reaction and the room in the moment.

adrian lyne.note: American director of Flashdance, Fatal Attraction, 9½ Weeks and Indecent Proposal — the go-to guy for glossy '80s/'90s erotic thrillers; Unfaithful (2002) is one of his later, less-discussed entries in that lane.

pier paolo pasolini.note: Italian poet-turned-director; Teorema (this film's Italian title) is his most controlled provocation — a mysterious stranger seduces every member of a bourgeois family, then vanishes, unraveling each of them differently.

abbas kiarostami.note: Iranian New Wave pioneer; this 1987 film (first of his loose Koker trilogy) is his breakthrough — a boy's small odyssey to return a classmate's notebook, deceptively simple and genuinely moving.

nation of language.note: Brooklyn synth-pop trio doing earnest, era-accurate New Order/early Human League worship — the more interesting reason to show up early on this bill if you like that cold-wave-gone-warm sound.

salute.note: Austrian-born, Brighton-based producer signed to Ninja Tune — fast, soulful house with a UK garage-adjacent bounce; has been playing bigger US festival stages (EDC) this year.

chloëdees.note: LA-based DJ and radio host known for genre-blending, eclectic sets rather than a single lane — less pedigree info available, so treat as the wildcard on this bill.

paul verhoeven.note: Before RoboCop/Total Recall/Basic Instinct, Verhoeven made kinky, Catholic-guilt-soaked Dutch thrillers — The 4th Man is the clearest preview of the button-pushing instincts he'd bring to Hollywood.

ernst lubitsch.note: Mostly known for the light comic touch (Ninotchka, The Shop Around the Corner) — Broken Lullaby is his one dead-serious drama, a 1932 anti-war film with none of the usual wit.

alex from tokyo.note: Paris-born, Tokyo-then-NY-based selector — Yellow Productions alum (compiled their Art of Disco series), eclectic deep house/disco crossover with a global-digger streak.

tony watson.note: LA house/disco DJ-producer (half of Project Sandro, runs the Adult Contemporary and American Standard labels) — an LA Weekly Best DJ pick and a Bar Franca regular.

juan nunez.note: LA underground house vet since the '90s — co-founded WAX Records with Doc Martin out of their Melrose shop, refined soulful selector still holding down a weekly stream.

spank rock.note: Baltimore rapper/producer (Naeem Juwan) out of Diplo's Hollertronix crew — 2006 debut YoYoYoYoYo (Big Dada) fused Bmore club/booty bass with rap, plus a satirical Benny Blanco collab EP; raunchy, dance-floor-first energy, not a straight hip-hop bill.

hadone.note: French producer, one half of the live hardware duo Civic Instruction — raw, 90s-flavored techno.

ufo95.note: French producer, the other half of Civic Instruction with Hadone — dark, hypnotic hardware-techno live sets; the pair just launched their own label, TSSRCT.

rob tregenza.note: American structuralist filmmaker — Talking to Strangers (1988) is his triple-threat debut (writer/director/cinematographer): nine unbroken 10-minute 35mm takes, shot once each, sequenced by computer-randomized order. The NYT called it an antidote to jazzy montage; a genuine formalist curio, not a normal narrative feature.

sarah register.note: LA experimental guitarist who plays in Kim Gordon's live band and co-produced her Grammy-nominated 'The Collective' — cut her teeth in NYC avant-pop duo Talk Normal (a Sonic Youth/Wire favorite) and is also a Grammy-nominated mastering engineer (Black Midi, Faye Webster).

sleepie louie.note: UK-born, LA-based rapper/artist (Louie Hillcoat) — thin public footprint beyond opener billings, so take this one as a wildcard support slot.

2hollis.note: LA-raised rage-rap/hyperpop artist (Hollis Frazier-Herndon) on Interscope — self-produced, genre-blurring pop/rap/EDM chaos out of the Playboi Carti/Opium orbit, not a house/techno name.

frost children.note: NYC sibling duo (Angel & Lulu Prost) splicing hyperpop, EDM, Jersey club and bloghouse into overclocked pop — their newest EP leans hardstyle/trance; more festival-pop chaos than a DJ set.

snow strippers.note: Detroit-formed electroclash duo (Tatiana Schwaninger & Graham Perez, Surf Gang/Mad Decent) doing bleary electro-pop shot through with witch house, trance and hardstyle — indie-sleaze revival energy, not house/techno.

underscores.note: SF-born, NYC-based producer April Harper Grey — genre-hopping hyperpop/indie/dubstep project (Mom + Pop), started on dubstep SoundCloud as a teenager; outside the house/techno lane but a real, well-reviewed act.

mcr-t.note: Berlin rapper/producer (Viktor Macha) out of the Live From Earth crew — raps live over a raw hip-hop/hard-techno/ghettotech hybrid; a genuinely different texture than a straight DJ set.

oppidan.note: UK garage producer, one of the faster-rising names in the current UKG wave — blends 2-step with 4x4 NUKG and bass; the garage-leaning name on an otherwise bass/EDM-heavy bill.

ranger trucco.note: Michigan-born tech-house producer/vocalist, Space Yacht signee — clean, warbling tech-house with his own sung hooks; the more house-adjacent name on a festival-bass-heavy bill.

rocket rese.note: LA-adjacent producer working rawstyle/gangsta-rap-inflected hard dance — couldn't verify much beyond recent streaming output, so treat as a minor supporting name.

geoboi.note: LA DJ with a thin public bio but a real footprint on the Echo Park/queer-underground circuit (played Sorbet at TBA - Echo Park alongside Shane Thomas) — a dancefloor-first selector.

banoffee.note: Melbourne-born, LA-based alt-pop producer/singer (Martha Brown) — SOPHIE collaborator and Charli XCX/Empress Of/King Princess associate with deep roots in the queer club circuit; more pop-production pedigree than a straight DJ.

captain planet.note: LA DJ/producer (Charlie Wilder) known for eclectic, high-energy sets blending Afrobeat, Latin, funk, disco, reggae and house — releases on Bastard Jazz; a genuine crate-digger's crate-digger.

latroit.note: Dennis White — Detroit-rooted, LA-based house producer since the late '80s (Berklee grad); won a 2018 Grammy for Best Remixed Recording on his Depeche Mode 'You Move' remix and runs the House of Latroit label/podcast.

rikhter.note: Yakutsk-born, Berlin-based hard/hypnotic techno producer signed to Kobosil's R Label Group — reverberating kicks and rolling, high-tempo intensity; Berghain resident-caliber, plays Rotterdam Rave and ADE.

emiliana.note: LA-based hard-techno producer/DJ, founder of the CTHRTC label and a WORK Harder (6AM Group) resident — distorted drums and ominous, experimental-noise-inflected techno.

mcr t.note: Berlin rapper/producer who raps live over a hip-hop/hard-techno/ghettotech hybrid — a different texture than a straight DJ set.

zen freeman.note: LA-based, London-raised DJ/producer who's built a career on the luxury-brand/celebrity circuit (Gucci, Vogue, the Oscars) but does have real house pedigree — releases on Defected, West End and Atlantic; expect a synthwave-tinted, crowd-pleasing set rather than a digger's night.

things you say.note: LA club-scene DJ project posting house mixes and playing local nights — low profile, nothing more substantial to verify beyond that.

ultra naté.note: Baltimore club/house vocalist behind '90s anthem 'Free' — a real voice of that Yoshitoshi/Deep Dish-adjacent house era, not a manufactured pop act.

crystal waters.note: NYC deep-house vocalist — 'Gypsy Woman (She's Homeless)' and '100% Pure Love,' both Basement Boys productions, are genuine foundational house-anthem catalog.

robin s.note: UK house vocalist whose 'Show Me Love' (1993) is one of the most sampled/replayed piano-house records ever — a real genre landmark even if the name itself isn't a household one.

myveronica.note: LA emotional-rock band dropping their debut LP 'I Hope There's Music in Heaven' on Sunday Drive Records the night of this show — channels Mineral/Sunny Day Real Estate-style emo with Sonic Youth-y noise-guitar.

young lovers.note: LA post-rock/shoegaze four-piece (Anxiety Blanket Records) — dense, guitar-driven and increasingly orchestral on their new record 'The Circle's End.'

big scary indian.note: Brooklyn duo (Roshan Reddy + Cheikh Proctor) playing splintery, hardcore-inspired art/noise-rock with wild rhythm changes — a good touring fit for a Smell bill.

matias aguayo.note: Chilean-German producer, ex-Kompakt (Closer Musik) — founded Cómeme in 2009, a label built on playful, vocal-forward, Latin-American-inflected minimal house/techno ('Rules' is the signature track); a genuinely distinctive, European-pedigree booking.

steven g.note: Bay Area hip-hop MC known for tracks like 'Pull Up' and 'Bag' — smooth, narrative-driven flow (not the Miami freestyle DJ who shares the name).

tayy tarantino.note: Anchorage, Alaska rapper — a rare touring booking from a small but real regional scene; has opened for Nas and Wu-Tang Clan up north.

pofsky.note: LA-via-805 singer/songwriter signed to Eric Bellinger's All Wins Entertainment — melodic, R&B-leaning hip-hop; also co-runs UNDRGRND Magazine.

brigid dawson.note: Longtime Thee Oh Sees/Osees co-vocalist and keyboardist who left the band years ago and has just rejoined for this LA residency run, revisiting songs from the Carrion Crawler/Help era; also has a solo career (2020's Ballet of Apes).

george chen.note: Likely the Bay Area experimental/noise musician and longtime scene organizer (Zum zine/label, bands like Chen Santa Maria) — a fittingly oddball opener rather than a straight rock act.

mexican institute of sound.note: Camilo Lara's long-running Mexico City project — cumbia, mambo and sonidero samples run through electronic production; a Latin Grammy-nominated producer and former EMI Mexico exec who co-founded Suave Records.

queen serene.note: Austin four-piece (Sarah Ronan, Matt Galceran, Riley Corcoran, Dale Pohly) playing hazy, synth-tinged shoegaze — self-titled debut album out in 2023.

katseye.note: Six-member multinational girl group formed via HYBE and Geffen's reality competition 'The Debut: Dream Academy' — K-pop-style idol pop, not a band.

xg.note: Japan-formed, LA-based girl group under XGALX doing hip-hop/R&B-leaning idol pop, sung mostly in English.

rich brian.note: Indonesian rapper and original 88rising signee, broke out with 2016's viral 'Dat Stick.'

umi.note: Seattle-born R&B/neo-soul singer-songwriter — the closest thing on this bill to her jazz/soul lane.

warren hue.note: Indonesian rapper on 88rising with a laid-back, melodic hip-hop style.

will swinton.note: Auckland-born, now LA-based pop songwriter — bedroom-pop turned Capitol signee, gravelly-voiced and TikTok-friendly; drew notice from Machine Gun Kelly after a chance meeting.

chico detour.note: Seattle garage-rock band with an EP ('Wash It Down') out on Den Tapes — a small touring DIY act, not an LA regular.

sizzy rocket.note: Queer alt-pop artist blending punk attitude with pop hooks — genre-blending electropop/pop-rock, profiled by Office Magazine for her unapologetic queer pop stance.

dor wand.note: dublab resident (Open Heart Social Club) and Basement-affiliated ambient artist/DJ — opens sets in live ambient before shifting into soulful house and Balearic, literally this party's own format.

sonrisita.note: dublab resident and record digger (Melissa Dueñas) behind Lowrider Sundays and the Eastside Story Project — boogie, disco and soul rooted in SoCal oldies culture.

natuta.note: Tbilisi/LA DJ and co-founder of eau_de_cologne_tbs, the queer party series tied to Georgia's Bassiani club scene.

mario liberti.note: Peru-born DJ who cut his teeth in Miami (residencies at Techno Loft, Club Space, Un_Mute) and is now based between Lima, Miami and Paris — founder of Deep In Dis, the label/party series this showcase is named for; deep, hypnotic techno and house.

chemtrail johnny.note: SoCal DJ/producer working in minimal, laid-back house and techno grooves — low profile but a real local scene name.

la luz.note: Shana Cleveland-fronted four-piece known for reverb-drenched, surf-noir garage rock with tight vocal harmonies — a real touring band, not a local cover act.

dj nu mark.note: Jurassic 5's turntablist and a prolific crate-digging producer/DJ who blends hip-hop, funk and global sounds in his sets.

ethio cali.note: LA ensemble led by Todd Simon fusing '60s-'70s Ethiopian jazz and funk through a California lens — marking 15 years together at this show.

miki yamanaka.note: Japan-born, NYC-based jazz pianist whose six-year-running trio (Tyrone Allen II, Jimmy Macbride) records this new album 'Breathe,' expanded here with saxophonist Nicole Glover.

nicole glover.note: acclaimed NYC tenor saxophonist — member of Christian McBride's Ursa Major and the all-star band ARTEMIS (two recent Blue Note releases), known for a clear, muscular tone.

jimmy macbride.note: Juilliard-trained NYC drummer who's played with Herbie Hancock and Wynton Marsalis; part of Yamanaka's regular working trio.

adam x.note: Brooklyn techno veteran since the early '90s, running the long-standing Sonic Groove label/party out of NYC's underground hardcore-into-techno lineage.

setaoc mass.note: Manchester-born, Berlin/Kyiv-based techno producer (SK_Eleven label) — sleek, hypnotic techno with IDM roots, a regular at Berghain and Bassiani.

marie nyx.note: LA-based DJ/producer (Delusional Records, Synr Records) blending electro, techno and darkwave-leaning experimental sounds; has played this same WORK series plus HARD Summer and CRSSD.

simon raymonde.note: bassist of Cocteau Twins and founder of the influential UK label Bella Union (Fleet Foxes, Beach House); 'Heaven or Los Angeles' riffs on the Cocteau Twins album title for a dream-pop/4AD-adjacent DJ set.

muku.note: Thin public footprint — mostly turns up as Fabiano do Nascimento's regular DJ-set opener/closer (also played alongside him at Chicago's Constellation), so treat this as a wildcard low-key close rather than a known quantity.

dj tennis.note: Manfredi Romano — Italian scene godfather who founded Life and Death in 2010 (Tale Of Us, Mind Against and Carlita all came up through the label); a globally touring, melodic house/techno selector with real ties to the Innervisions crowd via the Rakastella festival.

kaz james.note: Australian DJ/producer with old-school pedigree — a decade-long Pacha Ibiza residency (Nic Fanciulli's 'We Are The Night') behind him, now making straight-up house that's charted with tracks like 'Not in Love' and 'Footprints.'

propersoundco.note: No clear public bio surfaced — reads as this session's co-presenting sound/production crew (the 'Vol. 2' branding) rather than a separate DJ booking; can't verify further.

capes.note: LA underground house DJ/producer (Ray Barragan), half of club tularosa — small-room circuit, emotionally-charged sets over pure peak-time function.

sinéad.note: Reads as a San Francisco-based selector — groove-forward, house-heavy, hypnotic sets. Couldn't confirm this is the same Sinéad playing LA regularly, so treat as unverified.

floorplan.note: Robert Hood & daughter Lyric Hood — Detroit techno royalty (M-Plant) turned deep, gospel-inflected house. 'Baby Baby' fills a floor for a reason.

honeyluv.note: Cleveland-born, ex-Navy — one of the biggest tech-house breakouts of the last few years; soulful, groovy end of the genre, runs her own 4 Tha Luv label.

coco and breezy.note: Twin sisters (also the eyewear-brand founders) turned house/dance DJ duo — danceable, R&B-tinged, more crossover-pop energy than underground.

strawbry.note: LA underground fixture (South Florida-raised) — breaks-and-house sets, runs the STUDIO5400 party series.

vieze asbak.note: Dutch 'memecore'/troll-rave artist out of Amsterdam's Pestcore Collectief — hard-dance-adjacent chaos, not clean house or techno. A sign this bill gets weird in spots.

jazzy irl.note: Couldn't pin down a confident bio for this one — flagging as unverified rather than guessing.

kim anh.note: LA queer-underground institution, two decades deep — classic house, garage, minimal-wave leaning; founded the beloved Booby Trap! party and Can U Not Talk Records.

physical therapy.note: Daniel Fisher — Queens-via-Berlin producer known for genre-hopping, slightly off-kilter techno (bongo-flecked, breakbeat-inflected); runs Allergy Season and holds a residency at Nowadays. Real cult following, not a big-room name.

casmalia.note: LA-based bass/tech-house producer on a real hot streak — DoLab stage at Coachella, EDC Vegas, Splash House, direct support for Kyle Watson/Noizu/Diplo, and a track that hit #1 trending on SoundCloud US in late 2025. Festival-friendly, bass-heavy energy rather than deep/vinyl selecting.

emmber.note: LA-based house/techno producer and engineer; thin public footprint beyond production credits, so treat as a supporting local booking rather than a draw.

dj holographic.note: Detroit DJ/producer (Ariel Corley) blending house, disco, Motown, and techno — 2025 debut album 'House In The Dark' leans into Afrofuturism; praised by Carl Craig and The Blessed Madonna, has played Panorama Bar and Smart Bar.

colored craig.note: LA DJ known for soul/funk/jack-leaning house sets — a regular guest at A Club Called Rhonda over the years.

gay felony.note: LA DJ/producer (Melody Scallion) — extended vinyl sets ranging from soulful/progressive house to hard house and melodic techno; hosts a Dublab radio show.

anastazja.note: LA-based DJ (USC grad) who came up through Soulection Radio, played Boiler Room, and recently supported Keinemusik's Rampa — a credential that tracks with the melodic/Keinemusik lane.

axel boman.note: Swedish producer and Studio Barnhus co-founder — playful, eclectic deep house with a loose, jammy feel (his 'Purple Drank' and marathon festival sets are genre-defining); this is basically his label's home-turf party.

kornél kovács.note: Studio Barnhus co-founder alongside Axel Boman — bright, melodic, disco-tinged house; one of the most purely fun-first DJs in the European house scene.

secondcity.note: UK house producer behind 2014's global hit 'I Wanna Feel' and a Grammy-nominated remixer (Fall Out Boy's 'Centuries') — polished, vocal-driven house that's toured festival mainstages for a decade; he and Noizu have a track together ('More Love'), so this pairing tracks.

matthew dear.note: Ghostly International's flagship artist since the early 2000s (also records minimal techno as Audion) — moody, baritone-vocal art-pop laid over deep, European-club-respected production; a real crossover between listening-room songwriting and functional techno.

the juan maclean.note: John MacLean's long-running DFA Records project (James Murphy's label, home of LCD Soundsystem) — NYC dance-punk-turned-disco, best known for 'Happy House'; DJ sets lean house and post-punk-inflected disco.

mesme.note: LA-based (via the Midwest and Singapore) DJ and Into the Woods resident with a monthly dublab show — vinyl-heavy sets blending house, techno, acid, electro and trip-hop; a 2021 Boiler Room appearance and a 2020 EP on Steel City Dance Discs.

aali rehman.note: San Diego-based DJ/producer working deep house, melodic techno and dark disco — thin public footprint, and unclear how regularly they play LA.

wavves.note: Nathan Williams' surf-punk/lo-fi indie project out of San Diego — bratty, noise-caked guitar pop since 2008's 'Wavvves'; a real touring name with an actual catalog, not a local opener.

waax.note: Brisbane, Australia post-punk/garage band fronted by Marie 'Maz' DeVita — raw, emotive, three albums deep (most recently 2026's 'Angel's Mess').

the paranoyds.note: LA garage-rock/indie-punk four-piece out of the local DIY scene — Bratmobile-meets-Go-Go's energy, Third Man-affiliated, played Coachella and opened for Jack White.

modern color.note: Redondo Beach four-piece that started as metalcore and evolved into 'grungegaze' — alt-rock with shoegaze/hardcore edges, in the Hum/Title Fight/Deftones lineage.

korolova.note: Olga Korolova — Ukrainian melodic-techno/progressive-house producer, ex-ballet dancer turned DJ; runs the Captive Soul label/radio show, plays Tomorrowland mainstage and EDC, DJ Mag top-60 (2024).

spice aku bianca maieli dj sudi mtooray.note: LA DJ crew/event series/label built around their shared South Asian heritage — sets range Baile Funk to Bollywood, reggaeton to amapiano, dabke to dancehall; high-energy global club music, not a house/techno night.

ben annand.note: LA electronic scene fixture since the mid-'90s — longtime resident at Moontribe and founder of the Tropical party series (boats, warehouses, the desert); Balearic/tribal-leaning outdoor-party lane.

derrick carter.note: Chicago house legend since the late-'80s Warehouse/Muzic Box lineage — co-runs Classic Music Company with Luke Solomon; funky, genre-agnostic, unmistakable house selection still headlining at this level.

dj heather.note: Chicago house DJ, co-founder of the pioneering all-female Superjane crew (with DJ Colette, Dayhota, Lady D) — soulful, genre-blurring sets rooted in Gramaphone Records digging.

h foundation.note: San Diego duo (Hipp-E & Halo) — dub-inflected deep/tech-house with a Fabric London residency and a Chemical Brothers remix credit to their name; not a frequent LA booking.

hector moralez.note: Oakland-raised, now LA-based house DJ/producer (Minority Music, The Factory labels) — Chicago/Detroit-rooted, soul-deep selections; a regular in Sneak's LA circle.

j dub.note: Chicago-bred new-school house DJ and frequent DJ Sneak collaborator on the LA circuit (CHI♡LA, Certified Groovers) — funky, percussive, seamless-blend style.

jimi jules.note: Zurich-born, Berlin-based (longtime Watergate resident) house producer now signed to Innervisions — jazzy, soulful, musician's-ear house that broke through via 2014's Defected hit 'Pushing On.'

andy oro.note: LA DJ, host of the Oro Hour on VPN Radio and a Made to Move resident — eclectic underground/house sets pulling from DIY dance music, hip-hop and bloghouse.

knoxdotmp3.note: LA-based DJ/producer (KNOX) working house, ballroom and club sounds — released mix series like 'Club Cowboy' and played the VICE Underground 'Cage' night.

flabbergast la.note: LA techno DJ (Miami-raised, DIY rave background) and founder of VICE Underground — heavy drums, acid-driven, high-energy sets built for a transformative dancefloor, not a chill room.

buck off.note: LA DJ who's played Catch One, Los Globos and Avalon — moves from Chicago-style house by day to tech-house after dark; co-founded the Reverb party brand.

mayer hawthorne.note: Michigan-born, LA-based soul/R&B artist who broke via Stones Throw in the late 2000s — smooth blue-eyed soul with real digger credibility behind it, not just a nostalgia act.

kelly finnigan.note: Frontman of Bay Area deep-soul revivalists Monophonics and a well-regarded voice/producer in the current retro-soul scene.

the intruders.note: Philly soul group behind 'Cowboys to Girls' and 'I'll Always Love My Mama' — 60s/70s Gamble & Huff-era originals, not a tribute act.

blue magic.note: Philly soul group behind 'Sideshow' and 'Three Ring Circus' — genuine early-70s vocal-group pedigree on this bill.

joey quiñones.note: Frontman/producer of Thee Sinseers (Colemine Records) — the artist most credited with defining the modern Chicano lowrider 'souldies' revival out of Southern California.

denis dekay.note: Italian techno producer with releases on the well-regarded hard-techno label 999999999 and on No War Records — hypnotic, driving, festival-capable techno. This is a genuine first-ever US show, not a routine tour stop.

aiden ramos.note: LA DJ (Cal State Dominguez Hills, audio recording) and resident selector for Amore Disco — sets move through Balearic, house, disco and rare Italo with deep melodic touches; has played Berlin and Barcelona.

reedster.note: Amore Disco's other resident at Apotheke, playing alongside Aiden Ramos on the room's all-vinyl system — a reliable groove/disco selector, not a touring name.

bones.note: Co-resident (with Lee Wells) of House Heads, the long-running house night at Sound Nightclub in Hollywood -- LA house DJ/producer who's held that residency for years.

lee wells.note: LA-born house DJ/producer, House Heads co-resident since 2011 with residencies at several of LA's top clubs; played Coachella in 2014. Solidly in the LA house-scene establishment, not an underground unknown.

dj perception.note: London (Camberwell) 2-step/UK garage specialist and MoodSwing label head, drawing on 90s US house, garage and jungle — genuine scene pedigree (RA podcast feature, Fresh Milk dubplates), not a hype booking.

louiv.note: SF-based selector and founder of Texture Summit, a key Bay Area underground party/imprint since 2019 — punchy, groove-forward house and garage.

chris cruse.note: LA warehouse-scene DJ since 2001 and founder of Spotlight, the long-running queer-rooted house/techno/disco party — now Berlin-based, plays Panorama Bar and the festival circuit; a tough, sleazy, soulful sound.

soul purpose la.note: LA underground/festival selector (Splash House, Lightning in a Bottle, EDC) blending disco, 90s house, minimal, techno and hard groove — a dancefloor generalist more than a specialist.

alex ho.note: Pasadena-native LA DJ/producer — genre-bending sets spanning vintage boogie, proto-house and techno, plus a debut LP ('Move Through It') on the Dutch deep-digger label Music From Memory.

j rocc.note: LA turntablist and Beat Junkies co-founder, Stones Throw-adjacent — an eclectic crate-digger whose sets range across funk, soul, hip-hop and boogie. Genuine West Coast DJ royalty.

luxxury.note: LA producer Jason Kaplan's nu-disco/boogie alias — glossy, hook-forward throwback dance grooves, closer to Todd Terje's pastiche than straight house.

park jeong min.note: South Korean character actor (Bleak Night, Keys to the Heart, Deliver Us from Evil, Hellbound) — reliably one of the better performers in Korean genre cinema, not a marquee name most casual watchers will recognize.

terrell brooke.note: Founder of TheyHouse LA, a key figure in LA's queer house-music community — curates deep, Chicago-house-rooted lineups. This Sunday Sessions edition is explicitly billed as a celebration of house music's Black and LGBTQIA+ origins, not just a generic day party.

will worden.note: LA-via-Texas country/folk singer — Rolling Stone likened his voice to an Elvis/Gordon Lightfoot blend; his debut LP leans Countrypolitan, nodding to Lee Hazlewood and Glen Campbell.

same ol smile.note: LA country-boogie six-piece formed out of Mystic Braves and Jesus Sons — described as somewhere between the Flying Burrito Brothers and Captain Beefheart.

dj al lover.note: LA psych DJ/producer applying hip-hop sampling technique to the Thee Oh Sees / Ty Segall / White Fence garage-psych scene — a Desert Daze and Levitation Fest regular.

david moscoe.note: The Dresden's house bandleader — his trio anchors the venue's biweekly no-cover jazz/crooner nights alongside rotating singers.

dinabn.note: LA-based DJ affiliated with Club Cielo's Latin American-underground femme collective — limited verifiable bio beyond that affiliation.

voltage.note: UK DnB DJ/producer (real name Rouen Wilkins), one-third of Kings of the Rollers — decade-plus career, versatile across jump-up, jungle and deeper rollers.

ac13.note: Brighton-via-Bristol DnB producer on the rise — releases on Crucast, DnB Allstars and Tomorrowland Music; runs his own label Alpha Circuit.

archie hamilton.note: London DJ/producer/label owner — an early architect of a rugged, atmospheric minimal-house-and-techno sound; MicroHertz label boss and a Paradise Ibiza regular.

dj jenny lsq.note: Resident selector for Sid the Cat's recurring 'Freak Scene' night — free, all-ages indie/punk/old-school record sets in the venue's classroom-turned-lounge bar.

david harness.note: Bay Area deep-house DJ/producer/remixer (credits with Mary J. Blige, Alicia Keys) — soulful, classic house across Coachella, Glastonbury and beyond.

big cee.note: Chris Legaspi — the longtime resident opening DJ at Marques Wyatt's DEEP, a foundational figure in LA's house community who's shared decks with Frankie Knuckles and Louie Vega.

seeps.note: Bronx-born, LA-based DJ steeped in NYC's '90s golden-era house and disco/boogie — has drawn attention from Louie Vega and DJ Sneak.

kublaii.note: Hillsboro, Oregon-raised, Salt Lake City-based indie singer-songwriter blending folk, rock and electronic textures — 40M+ streams and a debut LP ('temujin') due in 2026.

steve von till.note: Neurosis co-founder/vocalist-guitarist — his solo work trades the band's crushing weight for dark, meditative acoustic folk and drone.

six organs of admittance.note: Ben Chasny's long-running psych-folk/drone project since the late '90s — a New Weird America mainstay, prolific collaborator (Comets on Fire, Rangda, MV & EE).

night beats.note: Seattle-formed psych/garage-rock band on The Reverberation Appreciation Society (Levitation's label) — fuzzed-out, surf-tinged garage with real touring chops.

brad mehldau.note: One of the most acclaimed jazz pianists of his generation — known for reharmonizing rock/pop songbooks (Radiohead, Nick Drake) through a jazz lens.

chris thile.note: Mandolin virtuoso, Punch Brothers/Nickel Creek — genre-crossing bluegrass-to-classical musicianship, former host of public radio's 'Live from Here.'

blake mills.note: In-demand guitarist/producer (Bob Dylan, Alabama Shakes, Perfume Genius) — a go-to for artful, texture-first arrangements.

powder.note: Tokyo DJ/producer Momoko 'Moko' Goto — eclectic, colorful disco/house/pop selector known for a widely-circulated Boiler Room Tokyo set.

dj healthy.note: NY-via-Tokyo selector, founder of the PACIFIC MODE party series — tripped-out house and tech.

daphni.note: Dan Snaith's (Caribou) dancefloor-focused alias, running his own Jiaolong label since 2012 — more raw and club-built than his Caribou records, with a strong Afro/global-rhythm bent.

roni size.note: Bristol jungle/DnB pioneer — Reprazent's 'New Forms' won the 1997 Mercury Prize; Full Cycle/Dope Dragon label boss. A legacy name that rarely turns up on a US warehouse bill.

dieselboy.note: Philadelphia DnB institution since the '90s (Human Imprint label) — first American voted into DJ Mag's Drum & Bass Arena top 10, first DnB artist to chart on Billboard's dance chart. Harder, darker end of the genre.

coffintexts.note: Miami producer (Alexandra Muggli) fusing Peruvian/Caribbean percussion with techno, bass and house — TraTraTrax/Club Romantico circle; off-kilter and sensual rather than straight peak-time.

trax unit.note: LA techno duo (Kyle Galindo & Kian Mahroo), Dublab residents and Gyration Station label founders — 90s-rooted, no-nonsense underground techno.

chris pavlov.note: LA vinyl DJ and Burnin' Chancla co-founder — plays warm, dug-up disco and house cuts channeling NYC dancefloor energy; the name behind this recurring hi-fi series.

ben sterling.note: London house/tech-house producer on Diynamic, Crosstown Rebels and Solid Grooves — disco-and-Chicago-house-rooted, championed by Jamie Jones and Patrick Topping.

dean turnley.note: Melbourne house producer working the Detroit/Chicago lineage — stripped, functional, dancefloor-built; broke out with 'Actin' Tough' hitting #1 on the Beatport chart.

walfredo reyes jr.note: Cuban-American percussionist — member of Santana, then Chicago's drummer/percussionist since 2012; decades on the road with Steve Winwood, Jackson Browne and Gloria Estefan. An arena-level name doing a rare, intimate father-daughter jazz-club set.

lucki.note: Chicago rapper who pioneered a melancholic 'alternative trap'/cloud-rap sound as a teenager (2013's Alternative Trap) — a real underground-to-indie-rap draw with a devoted following, well outside the house/techno lane.

jyoty.note: Indian-Dutch, London-based — Rinse FM resident and Boiler Room regular known for blending baile funk, amapiano, dancehall, jungle and UK garage into one set. Not house/techno, but a legitimately international name for a warehouse booking.

cquestt.note: Courtney Hollinquest — LA native, ex-touring backup dancer turned DJ who founded Baile World in 2020 as an Afro-Latina-led party fusing baile funk, reggaeton, dancehall and Black club music.

mango and ginger.note: Brazil-by-way-of-LA DJ duo built around baile funk and Afro-diasporic rhythms; best known for NYC's 'Favela Fridays' at SOB's, also play regularly on the LA/Baile World circuit.

stephanie rangel.note: Local South Pasadena selector with a standing residency at Sid's Bar; also plays disco sets at Let's Go! Disco & Cocktail Club downtown. Groove/disco-leaning, not a touring name.

yola.note: Youth Orchestra Los Angeles — the LA Phil/Dudamel-founded, El Sistema-inspired youth music program; performing alongside the full Phil here, not a separate act.

maxx steele.note: LA-based minimal-house producer/DJ — low profile, mostly plays local nights like this one; couldn't verify anything beyond that, so treat as an unknown quantity rather than a draw.

felix dickinson.note: UK DJ/producer out of the early-90s free-party scene — deep, chuggy, acid-tinged disco and house; runs Cynic Music, holds residencies at Glastonbury's Block9 and Houghton. A real European-disco-underground name, not a tourist booking.

skeme richards.note: Philadelphia-based DJ/collector with ~30 years digging funk & soul 45s — runs the all-45s party Hot Peas & Butta and is a genuinely respected name in vinyl-collector circles, not a random festival-flyer DJ.

naygod.note: Chicago-born, LA-based DJ/producer whose sets move through deep house, ghettotech, and techno; a regular at Akbar and General Lee's and around the LA underground/queer party circuit.

sepp.note: Minimal/tech-house DJ, producer, and label owner who's played Fabric London and Shelter/The Loft Amsterdam — a legitimate European-club-adjacent credit anchoring an otherwise TBA-location night.

degruvme miz honeyp and bella ferrada.note: The resident trio behind The Hustle's recurring global-disco / sexy-house / funk-soul sets at Gold Diggers — no individual bios turned up, but the free-door, 1st-and-3rd-Saturday residency is well documented.

laurel halo.note: Detroit-born, LA-based composer/producer — her 2012 Hyperdub debut 'Quarantine' was The Wire's Album of the Year; moves between techno, ambient and musique concrète rather than sitting in a DJ-set pocket.

baugruppe90.note: German techno duo (Louis Köhler & Paul Vogler) fusing 90s dnb/house/early-2000s-techno textures into a driving, industrial-leaning sound — releases on Sous Music, Steel City Dance Discs, and their own MONTAGE imprint.

partiboi69.note: Melbourne producer (Fintan Bradley) running his own Mutual Pleasure label — ghetto house, Miami bass, Detroit techno and ghettotech smashed together into loud, wild, high-energy sets; a real touring draw, not a support-slot name.

rebolledo.note: Mexico City producer, Cómeme label mainstay (Matias Aguayo's imprint) and half of Pachanga Boys — the duo behind 'Time,' a genuine Balearic-sunset anthem; his solo sets lean weirder — tribal, psychedelic, hypnotic house.

josh teed.note: Classically-trained violinist turned bass-music producer — live sets layer violin, didgeridoo and analog synth over DJ sets, in the Charlesthefirst/CloZee/Govinda festival-bass lineage.

pilo.note: LA producer/sound designer (aka Cameron Ward) — released on Turbo Recordings, has collaborated with Boys Noize; teaches this techno-production intensive at IO Music Academy.

george kahn.note: LA jazz pianist/composer reviving the 1950s-60s West Coast cool sound (Brubeck, Guaraldi lineage); this vocal-group Jazz & Blues Revue (singers Courtney Lemmon, Gina Saputo, Crystal Starr) is a regular Vibrato booking.

matt forbes.note: Jazz vocalist who took over Marty & Elayne's four-decade Dresden residency with co-host Jesse Goddard — an LA Times 'essential' pick for live jazz in LA.
